Evidence: messages unique index is (channel_id, sequence_number) and is NOT thread-aware. Thread replies allocate a per-thread counter starting at 1 (shared/core/thread-sequence.ts:21-29) but insert into the same messages table with the same channel_id. Replica insert is .onConflictDoNothing() with no target (:497) so ANY unique violation is swallowed.
Reproduction: Insert 1 channel message (seq 1) in channel C, then 1 thread reply in a thread of channel C (thread seq 1). The replica INSERT conflicts on (C,1) and onConflictDoNothing silently drops the thread reply from PG; no error, no outbox entry.
Root cause: Thread sequence space and channel sequence space both land in messages.sequence_number while the unique index is channel-scoped; onConflictDoNothing turns the collision into silent loss.
Impact: Thread replies permanently missing from the PG replica (RAG/context builders, multi-device sync); local tier still shows them so drift is invisible.
Proposed fix: Make the unique index thread-aware (e.g. partial index on channel_id + coalesce(thread_id, empty-string) + sequence_number) via migration and/or offset thread sequences per channel; keep onConflictDoNothing only after collision is impossible.
Required tests: Adapter test: append channel msg + thread reply with same logical seq, assert both rows exist in PG; migration test for new index; regression test for onConflict semantics.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-messages-micro-001-004): thread-aware unique index migration 0025 + schema.ts:315; targeted onConflictDoNothing(id) message-service.ts:566/708; regression test message-pagination.test.ts:181 red without target

Evidence: floorLocalSequenceFromReplica runs at most once per key per process and reads the replica head with the AMBIENT getDb() (:63-64), not the workspace-record DB handle used by the replica write (:488-489, :506-507). If channel history lives in a workspace DB while the ambient pool points elsewhere, the floor reads the wrong DB.
Reproduction: Workspace W has its own record DB; channel C history exists only in W DB. On a fresh process, appendMessage for C: floor reads ambient pool (different DB) and gets max 0, local counter restarts; the replica leg resolves W DB and adopts a seq that collides with W history; onConflictDoNothing silently drops the row.
Root cause: The floor bridge and the read gap-fill use the ambient handle while the write leg uses the workspace handle; tier resolution is per-workspace but the ambient pool is not that workspace DB.
Impact: After a process restart, local numbering can collide with workspace-DB history; replica rows are silently dropped (same silent-loss class as MSG-001).
Proposed fix: Resolve getWorkspaceDb(workspaceId) once and use it for floor + replica + read gap-fill; fall back to ambient only when no workspace DB exists.
Required tests: Two-DB harness test asserting floor reads the workspace head; restart-numbering regression.

Evidence: authorLevel is stored as String(input.authorLevel) (:396) but the returned row and message:new payload use the caller original value (:438, :468). ChannelMessage.authorLevel is typed AuthorityLevel | stakeholder while AppendMessageInput.authorLevel is string | number. The emitted payload is the DB row (has threadId/workspaceId), not the declared ChannelMessage.
Reproduction: Call appendMessage with authorLevel 2 (number) and inspect the returned object: authorLevel is 2 while a re-read from PG/local returns the string. Broker listeners typed against ChannelMessage receive extra fields.
Root cause: baseRow normalizes for storage but the return/emit path deliberately keeps the caller shape (comment :465-467); the declared event type was never widened to match.
Impact: Type-level drift only; consumers doing strict comparisons or relying on the declared payload type can misbehave.
Proposed fix: Either return the persisted shape everywhere or widen ChannelMessage/event payload types to the real row shape; add a broker payload type test.
Required tests: Contract test asserting returned row equals a re-read row for all fields; broker payload type test.

Evidence: mergeMessageRows pairs monologues/tool calls forward in time but runs on ONE page only (assemblePage reverses pageRows, merges, reverses back). A monologue whose final response is on the next (older) page becomes a synthetic Reasoning completed row on the newer page.
Reproduction: Seed a monologue row M (newer) and final agent row F (older). Page 1 (limit 50) includes M but not F so M surfaces as a synthetic monologue-agentId row. Page 2 includes F with no pending monologue. UI shows a stray card plus a bare final message.
Root cause: Pairing state is page-local; the read model has no cross-page continuity.
Impact: Duplicate/misplaced reasoning cards at page boundaries; thought attachment lost on the older page; visible UI artifact when scrolling.
Proposed fix: Fetch one overlap row and suppress boundary synthetic rows, or carry pairing state in the cursor, or attach thoughts to the raw row and let the client fold (client already folds tools, MainChatArea.tsx:711-784).
Required tests: Characterization test: monologue on page N, final on page N+1, assert one card and no synthetic row; boundary regression both directions.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-messages-micro-001-004): page-boundary pairing via older/newer context rows (message-service.ts:268/369/453/517); boundary test message-pagination.test.ts:311 red without fix (both halves neutered), in-flight guard :339

Evidence: The scheduler passes a stable jobId as message id for retry idempotency. appendMessage uses the id for the row and the replica insert is onConflictDoNothing (:497), but the LOCAL append (message-local-store.ts:88-94) has no id dedupe. A BullMQ retry after a local success appends a second JSONL line with the same id and a NEW sequence number.
Reproduction: Call appendMessage twice with the same id (simulating a retry). Local JSONL has two lines with the same id (different seq); PG has one row. Local-tier reads show the message twice.
Root cause: Local store is append-only with no uniqueness enforcement; idempotency was only designed into the PG leg.
Impact: Duplicate messages in local reads (desktop/local-first default) after scheduler/worker retries; PG stays clean so tiers diverge.
Proposed fix: Add id-based dedupe to localAppendMessage (scan or side index), or make the local seq allocation keyed by id, or have the scheduler check-before-append; document the chosen idempotency scope.
Required tests: Retry test: same id twice yields one local row and one PG row; worker retry integration test.

Evidence: listRecentMessages PG order is only timestamp DESC (:279), no sequenceNumber tiebreak, unlike getChannelMessagesPage (:302) and unlike the local path (seq tiebreak, message-local-store.ts:104-107). Rows sharing a timestamp can flip order between reads.
Reproduction: Insert two messages with identical timestamps; call listRecent repeatedly and observe order variance; context middlewares see inconsistent history order across calls.
Root cause: Tiebreak omitted in one of three ordering sites.
Impact: Unstable context assembly ordering; flaky roster derivation in channel-awareness-middleware.ts:45-60 which depends on order.
Proposed fix: Add desc(sequenceNumber) to the listRecent PG orderBy; add a parity test across all three ordering sites.
Required tests: Ordering test with identical timestamps for listRecent and the page path.

Evidence: GET /api/channels/:channelId/messages never compares the caller workspace (request.workspaceId) with the channel owning workspace. With x-workspace-id the tenant hook pins request.db to the caller workspace DB and the page query runs there; without the header the service resolves the channel workspace and serves its local/PG rows. The socket path by contrast denies cross-workspace joins (channel_forbidden, :564-566).
Reproduction: Caller authenticated for workspace A requests GET /api/channels/<channel-of-B>/messages. With the header the A-DB query returns nothing only because channel ids are globally unique. Without the header the local tier resolves B folder and serves B history to any authenticated caller.
Root cause: Transport-level tenant check missing on the REST read route; the domain trusts channel-id resolution. Multi-workspace isolation enforced only in sockets.
Impact: Cross-workspace history disclosure in local/no-header mode; dual mode relies on accidental global id uniqueness rather than policy.
Proposed fix: Route resolves the channel row and compares its workspaceId to request.workspaceId, rejecting mismatch with 403, mirroring the socket rule; add regression tests.
Required tests: Auth/isolation test: caller ws A to channel of ws B returns 403/404 on both tiers.

Evidence: normalizeStructuredInput JSON.stringifies args; buildToolCard sets status error only when output startsWith Error: prefix. A structured result that is a non-string object is String()-ed (:178) losing structure, and success detection is prefix-based on the string form. Legacy results with lowercase error prefix are marked success.
Reproduction: Store a structured call with result {ok:false} -> output becomes [object Object] and status success. Store legacy result starting with lowercase error -> status success.
Root cause: Heuristic prefix matching plus string coercion in the display mapper.
Impact: Wrong success/error badge for tool cards; lossy rendering of structured results.
Proposed fix: Prefer explicit result.ok/error fields when present; fall back to prefix matching only for legacy rows; JSON.stringify non-string results instead of String().
Required tests: Unit tests for structured object results, lowercase error, non-Error prefix cases.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-messages-micro-008-009): structuredResultStatus wired into the structured tool-call mapper message-service.ts:295 (explicit ok/error beats prefix; JSON.stringify preserves structure); regression test message-pagination.test.ts:383 (red before wiring).

Evidence: routes/threads.ts calls messageGate.append WITHOUT a broker (:98-107) then emits message:new itself via the global broker (:110-114). If append ever gains a broker every thread reply double-emits; today the domain emit path is bypassed for thread replies.
Reproduction: POST a thread message and count broker events: one, from the route. Add a broker to the append call in a future edit and there are two.
Root cause: Emission responsibility split between route and domain; the route comment says emit via global broker to avoid a cycle (:109).
Impact: Latent double-delivery (duplicate UI messages / double index counters) if append gains a broker; ownership violation (transport emits a domain event).
Proposed fix: Pass the broker into append and delete the manual emit, or document an explicit no-broker append variant.
Required tests: Regression test asserting exactly one message:new per thread post (count broker events).
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-messages-micro-008-009): route passes broker INTO messageGate.append and manual emit deleted routes/threads.ts:110-131; domain emits once message-service.ts:652/684/736; regression test message-pagination.test.ts:418 (red-check with manual emit -> 2 events).

Evidence: The read path gap-fill uses fetchPg(getDb()) (:313) while the write replica leg resolves the workspace-record DB. In dual mode with a workspace DB, a read for a channel whose local log is empty (first open after migration) never consults the workspace DB and returns an empty page although the replica has history.
Reproduction: Workspace W with its own DB; local log empty; GET messages for a channel with history in W DB. withStoreFallback sees empty local then fetchPg(getDb()) queries the ambient pool (different DB) -> empty page.
Root cause: Ambient-pool default vs per-workspace handle mismatch on the read path.
Impact: First-open empty history after migration; combined with MSG-002, restart numbering collisions.
Proposed fix: Resolve the workspace handle once via workspaceOfChannel + getWorkspaceDb and use it for the read gap-fill (fallback ambient when no workspace DB).
Required tests: Two-DB read test: empty local + workspace-DB history returns rows.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-messages-micro-010-011): read gap-fill resolves the workspace-record handle via resolveWorkspaceHandle(workspaceId) ?? getDb() message-service.ts:487 (was fetchPg(getDb()) ambient pool only); regression test message-pagination.test.ts:527 (red before wiring: empty page vs workspace-DB history). Evidence: npx vitest run src/messages (7 passed/5 skipped); npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit (clean).

Evidence: channelWorkspaceCache caches null results (hit check is !== undefined; :30-31). A channel that does not resolve on first lookup (created later, or a gate error caught at :32) pins ws=null until the cache clears past 5000 entries or the process restarts.
Reproduction: Lookup workspaceOfChannel for a not-yet-created channel, create the channel in ws-A, then append a message: input.workspaceId resolves null, so the row lands in the default workspace folder with no replica target.
Root cause: Negative caching without invalidation; channel creation never invalidates this cache.
Impact: Messages filed in the default workspace scope permanently; workspace isolation (INV-26) broken; cache clear is a blunt non-deterministic remedy.
Proposed fix: Do not cache null (or use a short TTL) and invalidate on channel create; prefer a lookup that also checks the log-file fallback.
Required tests: Test: pre-lookup an unknown id, create the channel, append, assert the row lands in the channel workspace scope.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-messages-micro-010-011): null results are never cached; positive-only memo + log-file fallback findWorkspaceIdForChannelLog message-service.ts:36-55 (was negative cache until clear/restart); regression test message-pagination.test.ts:607 (red with negative cache: lookup pinned null after channel resolves). Evidence: npx vitest run src/messages (7 passed/5 skipped); npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit (clean).

Evidence: appendMessage performs no validation of channelId/authorId/authorName/authorType/content. The socket path destructures content without checking (:688) and passes it (:745); only the threads route trims/validates.
Reproduction: Emit user:message with content undefined. Local: JSON.stringify drops the content key so the local row has no content; PG: NOT NULL violation -> replica failure -> outbox entry with a null-ish row.
Root cause: Validation lives inconsistently in transports; the domain gate has no schema.
Impact: Malformed rows or permanently failing replica entries; callers cannot rely on the gate to reject bad input.
Proposed fix: Add a zod schema for AppendMessageInput (validated in appendMessage or the gate), requiring non-empty channelId/authorId/authorName/authorType/content.
Required tests: Unit tests: each required field missing yields a typed rejection; socket integration test with empty content.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-messages-micro-012-018): appendMessageInputSchema (message-validators.ts:30) enforced in appendMessage before any write -> InvalidMessageInputError MESSAGE_INVALID_INPUT (message-service.ts:215/613-618); regression test message-pagination.test.ts:846 (5 fields, no local write). Socket-path test coverage tracked as NEXT_ACTION.

Evidence: MAX_PAGE_LIMIT (200) is exported from the service but not re-exported through the gate, while DEFAULT_PAGE_LIMIT is. The route enforces 1-200 independently in zod (message-validators.ts:6).
Reproduction: grep for MAX_PAGE_LIMIT outside message-service.ts: no matches; docs list it as a gap.
Root cause: Incomplete gate re-export.
Impact: Three places encode the 200 limit (service clamp, validator, docs); drift risk if one changes.
Proposed fix: Re-export MAX_PAGE_LIMIT through the gate and derive the validator max from it.
Required tests: Test asserting validator max equals MAX_PAGE_LIMIT.

Evidence: Limit clamp uses Math.trunc/NaN propagation: a NaN limit (direct caller) yields NaN; limit+1 NaN goes to PG .limit() or local slice.
Reproduction: Call getChannelMessagesPage with limit NaN directly (non-route caller): PG may error or ignore the limit; local slice(0, NaN) returns []. Behavior differs by tier.
Root cause: Missing Number.isFinite guard in the clamp.
Impact: Tier-dependent behavior for malformed direct calls; potential unbounded query if PG ignores NaN.
Proposed fix: Guard with Number.isFinite and fall back to DEFAULT_PAGE_LIMIT.
Required tests: Unit tests: NaN, 0, -1, 10^9 for both tiers.

Evidence: The REST route forwards request.db (tenant handle) which PINS PG and skips the local tier when the header is present, inverting the documented local-first read order.
Reproduction: Same channel: a request with x-workspace-id gets a PG-only page (may lag local writes during a replica outage); a request without the header gets a local-first page that includes local-only messages. Two clients see different history.
Root cause: The read path honors explicit db overrides by design (tests/seeds), but the route reuses it for normal tenant traffic.
Impact: Tier-dependent history views during replica lag; docs claim local-first reads.
Proposed fix: Route should not pin PG for normal reads, or the service should prefer local content even with a db override.
Required tests: Consistency test: a local-only message is visible to both header/no-header reads.

Evidence: Every structured tool call on one row emits id tool-msgId (:101). Multiple calls per row produce duplicate ids within one page.
Reproduction: Persist one monologue row with toolCalls a and b; read the page and find two cards with identical id. Client keying may collide.
Root cause: Card id derived from row id only; no call index or callId.
Impact: Duplicate keys in client render; anchor/scroll-to-message ambiguity.
Proposed fix: Include the call index or callId: tool-msgId-index or callId.
Required tests: Unit test: one row, two calls, unique ids.

Evidence: Synthetic leftover rows use a string ISO timestamp, authorLevel "3", authorName "Agent Swarm", and no sequenceNumber/mentions/isInternalMonologue; real rows use Date timestamps and numeric seq.
Reproduction: Persist a monologue-only tail with no final response; read the page and observe a synthetic row with a string timestamp. mapBackendMessage coerces via new Date (crowdOsStore.ts:491) so it survives, but code doing .getTime() on the raw field would crash.
Root cause: Synthetic display row never conformed to ChannelMessage.
Impact: Shape drift; downstream Date assumptions break; sequenceNumber-less rows interact with client seq bookkeeping (maxSeq reduce ignores them, crowdOsStore.ts:2874).
Proposed fix: Build synthetic rows to match ChannelMessage or declare a discriminated page-item type in ChannelMessagesPage.
Required tests: Type-level plus runtime test asserting every page item matches the declared union.

Evidence: message:new is emitted even when the PG replica leg failed (catch falls through to :525). Listeners such as IndexBuilder.incrementMessageCount treat the event as persisted.
Reproduction: Simulate a replica failure: the append succeeds locally, message:new fires, the index counter increments, but a consumer reading PG for the row finds nothing until outbox replay.
Root cause: Emit ordering versus replica outcome; local-first says emit after the commit point, but consumers assume event implies PG visibility.
Impact: Read-after-event skew: counter drift; clients fetching by seq from PG miss the message.
Proposed fix: Document the event as local-commit-only and fix consumers to read the local tier, or emit a distinct event on replica failure plus a replay compensation.
Required tests: Failure-injection test: replica failure emits once; consumer contract test.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-messages-micro-012-018): message:new documented as LOCAL-COMMIT event (message-service.ts:588-592); replica failure still emits exactly once with the row queued to the outbox (message-service.ts:759); regression test message-pagination.test.ts:896 (failure-injection: 1 emit + 1 outbox entry). Consumer-reads-PG contract (IndexBuilder counter) tracked as NEXT_ACTION.

Evidence: When opts.tx is provided, appendMessage emits message:new (:441) inside the caller transaction before the caller commits; a rollback after emit leaves an event for a row that never existed.
Reproduction: No in-tree tx callers today (grep). Latent for seeds/backfill tooling.
Root cause: Emit placed inside the tx branch after the inner write resolves.
Impact: Phantom events if a tx caller rolls back.
Proposed fix: Emit only after the caller signals commit, or document that tx callers must not pass a broker.
Required tests: Contract test once a tx caller exists; document in the domain spec now.

Evidence: Outbox replay for messages inserts the row with onConflictDoNothing by id (:445-450) but does NOT repair channel_sequences. repairPgCounter exists only for the bulk push path (:191-202, called at :264).
Reproduction: Replica leg fails after local commit (outbox queued). Later drain replays the insert into PG but channel_sequences.last_seq stays behind. A PG-side allocateSequence then reissues sequence numbers already present; unique violation and onConflictDoNothing drops rows silently.
Root cause: Counter repair is not part of per-entry replay.
Impact: Silent row loss for messages written by the PG-side allocator after a replay; cross-tier seq collisions.
Proposed fix: Add GREATEST counter repair to the message replay entry (same SQL as repairPgCounter).
Required tests: Failure-injection test: fail replica, drain outbox, allocate on the PG side, assert no collision.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-messages-micro-020-030): outbox replay for entity=message now repairs the PG counter via the same GREATEST upsert (repairPgCounter) as the bulk push and append replica legs - workspace-sync.ts:510-520; regression test message-pagination.test.ts:765 (red before wiring: 1 insert call vs 2). Evidence: npx vitest run src/messages (11 passed/5 skipped); npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit (clean).

Evidence: Local reads scan the whole channel JSONL and sort on every page request (O(n log n) per read; documented ponytail for single-user local mode). listRecent also scans on every context assemble.
Reproduction: 10k-message local channel: each page read re-parses the file; each agent turn scans the full log for 60 rows.

Impact: CPU/IO growth with channel size in local mode; slower agent turns on long histories.

Reproduction: Grep results in the inventory section 5/6.

Evidence: Replica failures are swallowed into console.warn plus an outbox entry with NO metric/span; the outbox is unbounded by design. A permanently failing replica surfaces only as a backlog notice past 100 entries in the Overview UI.
Reproduction: Kill the workspace DB, append 1000 messages, observe only console warnings and a backlog counter.
Root cause: No telemetry on the domain write path.
Impact: Silent replica drift; ops rely on the UI notice; no alerting hook.
Proposed fix: Add a metric/counter (replica failure count, outbox depth) and a structured log event.
Required tests: Observability test: replica failure increments a metric.

Evidence: seqFloored is process-local: a multi-process deployment (API+worker) floors independently; idempotent by design but combined with MSG-002 one process may floor against the wrong DB and the other not at all.
Reproduction: Run API and worker against the same workspace DB; with different ambient handles the worker may not floor.
Root cause: Process-local memo of a cross-process fact.
Impact: Inconsistent floors across processes; see MSG-002 impact.
Proposed fix: Fix MSG-002 first; then consider moving the floor into PG (allocateSequence already seeds from MAX for legacy channels).
Required tests: Covered by the MSG-002 tests.

Evidence: shared/core imports messages/message-local-store.localAllocateSequence directly. Shared is exempt per AGENTS.md and lint:gates reports 0 violations, but this couples the shared allocators to a messages implementation file, the reverse of the intended facade direction.
Reproduction: lint:gates output: 0 violations; grep shows the imports.
Root cause: Documented exemption used as a permanent bridge.

Required tests: Import-boundary test if the exemption is tightened.

Evidence: pendingMonologues is keyed by authorId and overwritten by the LATEST monologue (assignment at :202). If an agent emits two reasoning blocks before a final response, only the last survives; the earlier is dropped from display without a synthetic row.
Reproduction: Persist monologue A, monologue B, final F (same author, same page). The page shows F with metadata.monologue equal to B only; A is invisible.
Root cause: Single-slot pending buffer; no accumulation.
Impact: Lost reasoning content in the UI (display-only).
Proposed fix: Accumulate/join monologues per author, or emit one synthetic row per unpaired block.
Required tests: Unit test: two monologues plus final, both visible per the chosen contract.

Evidence: Legacy tool-result pairing consumes queued inputs by author plus tool name. With two calls to the same tool and only one result row in the page, the first input pairs and the second queued input is dropped at function end (no unmatched-input surfacing).
Reproduction: Persist a monologue with two read_file calls and one tool-result for read_file. The card pairs with call 1; call 2 disappears from display.
Root cause: Page-scoped pairing state with no unmatched-input surfacing.
Impact: Unmatched tool inputs silently disappear from the display.
Proposed fix: Surface unmatched queued inputs as pending cards or extend pairing across pages; decide the contract.
Required tests: Characterization test for unmatched calls.

Evidence: Socket user:message persists authorId from the verified identity (good), but appendMessage accepts ANY authorId/authorName from any caller and there is no ownership check that agent/system rows come from the right code. Any in-process caller can impersonate another author.
Reproduction: Any domain calling messageGate.append can write authorType system with authorName System Warning or authorType agent with another agent id.
Root cause: Trust boundary is at the transport, not the domain; the domain is an internal API.
Impact: Impersonation requires in-process code access (medium/low severity), but a buggy or compromised caller can forge history that RAG/UI treat as authoritative.
Proposed fix: Consider an optional internal actor check (system rows only with an actor option) or document the trust model in the domain spec.
Required tests: Unit test documenting the trust boundary.
